name: Shadrach
summary: A young man of Judah, first called Hananiah, who was trained in the court of Babylon with Daniel. With Meshach and Abednego he refused to worship the king's golden image, and God brought them out of the furnace unharmed.

key_moments.title: Renamed Shadrach in Babylon
key_moments.description: Hananiah was among the young men of Judah taken into the king's court, and was given the name Shadrach. He and his friends ate vegetables and drank water instead of the king's food, and God gave them knowledge and wisdom.

key_moments.title: Set Over Babylon
key_moments.description: When the king's dream was a secret, Daniel asked Shadrach and his friends to pray to God for mercy. After Daniel told the dream, the king put the three in charge of Babylon's affairs.

key_moments.title: Refusing to Bow
key_moments.description: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and ordered everyone to worship it. Shadrach and his friends told the king their God was able to save them, but even if He did not, they would not bow.

key_moments.title: Saved from the Fiery Furnace
key_moments.description: The three were tied up and thrown into a furnace heated seven times hotter. The king saw four men walking free in the fire, and they came out without even smelling of fire, so he praised their God and promoted them.
